prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” lawyer for every car-wreck case — the right attorney depends on your specific facts (injuries, fault dispute, insurance limits, whether the other driver is represented, need to sue a government entity, etc.). I can help you find the strongest lawyer for your situation if you tell me a ZIP code and a few case details. Meanwhile, here’s how to find and pick the best Houston personal-injury lawyer for a car wreck:

Key qualifications to look for
- Trial experience in serious car-crash cases (not just settlements). Many good cases are resolved without trial, but you want someone who will try the case if needed.  
- Board certification or recognized peer-review ratings (e.g., Texas Board of Legal Specialization, AV Preeminent from Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers).  
- Track record of meaningful settlements/verdicts for injuries similar to yours (fractures, spinal injuries, brain injuries, etc.).  
- Reasonable contingency fee and clear fee agreement (typical Texas contingency 33–40% if case settles before suit).  
- Good communication: returns calls/emails, explains strategy and timelines.  
- Local Houston courtroom experience and knowledge of local judges and insurers.

Where to search and verify credentials
- Houston Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.  
- Texas State Bar website (lawyer directory and disciplinary records).  
- Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, National Trial Lawyers, and client reviews on Google/Yelp.  
- Ask friends/family or other lawyers for local referrals.

Questions to ask in the free consultation
- Do you handle car-accident cases full time? How many per year?  
- Have you tried similar cases to verdict? Examples? (Ask for outcomes.)  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day — you or someone else in the firm?  
- What is your fee structure and estimated costs?  
- What is your estimated value range for a case like mine and expected timeline?  
- How often and by what method will you update me?

Immediate practical steps
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicle damage and injuries, witness info, medical records, and police report number.  
- Don’t sign releases from insurers or agree to recorded statements without counsel.  
- Get prompt medical care and follow treatment — gaps can hurt your claim.  
- Be aware: Texas generally has a 2-year statute of limitations for personal-injury suits (there are exceptions), so don’t delay seeking counsel.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of well-rated Houston firms/attorneys (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood).  
- Give a tailored checklist of documents to bring to a consultation.  
Tell me where you are (ZIP or neighborhood) and one or two details about the crash (injury severity, fault dispute, insurance coverage), and I’ll suggest 3–5 lawyers/firms to contact.
